description: Unique alphanumeric identifier for each chatbot conversation session (format: S followed by 4-digit zero-padded number). Each session represents one student interaction with the chatbot.
Date and time when the student query was submitted, formatted as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS. Timestamps are sequential and reflect realistic university operating hours.

Categorical classification of query complexity level. query_type_1 = simple FAQ lookup, query_type_2 = specific information request, query_type_3 = procedural/how-to question, query_type_4 = status/deadline inquiry, query_type_5 = complex multi-part or complaint-type query.

The NLP-classified intent category of the student query. Valid values: admissions (enrollment/admission process), exams (examination schedules/results/rules), fees (tuition/payment/refunds), hostel (accommodation/mess/facilities), grievance (complaints/anti-ragging/redressal), library (books/resources/timings).

Model confidence score for the intent classification, ranging from 0.0 (no confidence) to 1.0 (full confidence). Scores below 0.60 indicate ambiguous or unclear queries. Mean score across dataset is approximately 0.80.

Binary flag indicating whether the query was escalated to a human support agent. 0 = resolved by chatbot autonomously, 1 = escalated to human agent. Escalation typically occurs when confidence is low or the query involves sensitive grievance/complaint matters. Approximately 3-5% of queries are escalated.

Student satisfaction rating for the chatbot response on a 1-5 Likert scale. 1 = Very Dissatisfied, 2 = Dissatisfied, 3 = Neutral, 4 = Satisfied, 5 = Very Satisfied. Used to measure chatbot effectiveness and identify areas for improvement.
